User manual

R U OK?

A wellness check-in system for people who live alone. A small sensor box in the home reports motion and sound to a local server; guardians watch status and receive alerts in a mobile app or web portal.

Version 0.2.0 Prepared 2 September 2026 Platforms Windows server · Android app · Raspberry Pi device

1System overview

R U OK? answers one question for a guardian: has there been any sign of life in the home recently? It does this without cameras and without recording audio. The device only reports that motion or sound occurred and when.

Roles

Monitored person
Lives with the device. Needs to do nothing.
Guardian
Family member or carer. Registers devices, sets schedules and thresholds, receives and acknowledges alerts.
Operator
Runs the server on a Windows PC on the home network and installs the device.

2Requirements

ComponentNeeds
ServerWindows 10/11 with Python 3.11 or newer and PowerShell. Roughly 50 MB of disk. Port 8787 open on the local network.
Guardian appAndroid 8.0 (API 26) or newer. To build from source: Flutter 3.35 with the Android SDK.
DeviceRaspberry Pi Zero 2 WH (or any Pi with Wi-Fi) running Raspberry Pi OS, Python 3.9+, an HLK-LD2410C radar module and a USB microphone. Mock mode needs no sensors.
NetworkServer, phone and Raspberry Pi on the same Wi-Fi network. The server uses plain HTTP; it is intended for a home LAN, not the public internet.

3Quick start

The order matters: the server must exist before the app can sign in, and a device must be registered in the app before the Raspberry Pi can report.

  1. Start the serverOn the Windows PC run web\setup_server.ps1 once, then web\run_server.ps1 with RUOK_HOST=0.0.0.0. Note the PC's IP address from ipconfig.
  2. Install the guardian appInstall the APK on the phone. Open Server settings, enter http://<PC IP>:8787, and tap Save and test connection.
  3. Create a guardian accountTap New here? Create an account, enter a name, email and password. Registration signs you in immediately.
  4. Register a deviceTap Add device. Copy the device_uid and device_token. The token is shown only once.
  5. Set up the Raspberry PiCopy the device/ folder to the Pi, put the server URL, UID and token into config/config.json, and run python main.py. Start in mock sensor mode to verify the connection.
  6. Watch the dashboardWithin a minute the device shows Normal with a recent heartbeat. Set a sleep schedule and adjust thresholds if the defaults do not fit the household.

4Server

The server is a FastAPI application backed by a single SQLite file. It stores accounts, devices, events and settings, evaluates every device once a minute, and serves both the device API and the guardian API. It also hosts a small web portal.

4.1 Install and run

cd D:\2026_project\ruok\web
.\setup_server.ps1        # creates .venv, installs FastAPI + uvicorn, initialises the database
.\run_server.ps1          # starts on http://127.0.0.1:8787

Configuration is read from environment variables. Copy .env.example or set them in the shell before starting:

VariableDefaultMeaning
RUOK_HOST127.0.0.1Bind address. Use 0.0.0.0 so phones and devices on the LAN can connect.
RUOK_PORT8787TCP port.
RUOK_DBdata/ruok_server.sqlitePath of the SQLite database. Created on first start.
RUOK_SECRET_KEYbuilt-in dev valueKey used to sign guardian session tokens. Set a long random value for any use beyond a single developer's machine.

Confirm the server is up by opening http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/health in a browser. It returns {"ok": true, "service": "ruok-local-server", ...}.

4.2 Reaching it from a phone

$env:RUOK_HOST = "0.0.0.0"
$env:RUOK_PORT = "8787"
.\run_server.ps1
ipconfig     # find the IPv4 address of the Wi-Fi adapter, e.g. 192.168.1.25

If Windows Defender Firewall prompts on first start, allow access on private networks. If the phone still cannot connect, add an inbound rule for TCP port 8787.

USB alternative for testingWith the phone connected by USB and USB debugging enabled, run adb reverse tcp:8787 tcp:8787 and set the app's server address to http://127.0.0.1:8787. No Wi-Fi is needed.

4.3 Web portal

Open http://<PC IP>:8787/ in a browser. The portal offers the same functions as the app: register or sign in, create devices, view the status grid, set sleep schedules and presence modes, edit alert rules, view events and acknowledge alerts. A button labelled Evaluate alerts now runs the status check immediately instead of waiting for the 60-second loop.

5Guardian app

The Android app is the guardian's daily view. It keeps you signed in between launches and refreshes on pull-down.

5.1 Install and connect

Install the debug APK (app-debug.apk) from the project, or build it yourself:

cd app
flutter pub get
flutter build apk --debug
# build\app\outputs\flutter-apk\app-debug.apk

The first screen is Guardian sign in. Before signing in, tap the gear icon to open Server settings and point the app at your server. The default http://10.0.2.2:8787 only works inside the Android emulator.

Keep the tokenThe device_token is displayed once, right after creation. If it is lost, delete the device and create a new one.

5.2 Dashboard

Every registered device appears as a card with a coloured status badge, the server's one-line reason, the active mode, and how long ago motion and sound were last detected. The bell in the header shows the number of unacknowledged alerts, and the five most recent alerts are listed below the devices.

The menu in the top-right corner opens Server settings and Sign out. Signing out clears the stored session on the phone only.

5.3 Device detail

Tap a device card to open it. The top card shows the status the server computed for this device right now:

RowMeaning
Current modeHome, Sleep (inside the sleep schedule), or an active presence mode such as Away.
Last seenLast time the device contacted the server for any reason, including heartbeats.
Last motion / Last voiceLast detection of each kind, with a relative time.
No reaction forMinutes since the most recent motion, sound or button press. This is the number compared against the thresholds.
Battery, Wi-FiValues the device reports in its heartbeat metadata, if configured.

Below it are the three settings screens and the recent event log (motion, voice, heartbeat, button).

5.4 Sleep schedule, presence modes and alert rules

Sleep schedule

While the schedule is active, the server uses the longer sleep thresholds so that a full night without motion does not raise an alert. A schedule that crosses midnight (for example 22:30 to 06:30) is handled correctly. New devices start with 22:00 to 07:00 every day.

Presence modes

Use a preset when the person is out of the house. During Away, Vacation, Pause and Maintenance the server stops raising no-activity alerts and only checks that the device is online. Presets expire automatically after their duration; Back to home mode ends them early. If several modes overlap, the most restrictive wins: vacation, then away, then pause, then maintenance.

Alert rules

Five thresholds per device, all in minutes. Turning the switch off disables evaluation for that device entirely and shows Alerts off on the dashboard.

RuleDefaultRaises
Daytime warning threshold180Warning after this many minutes without motion, sound or a button press outside sleep time.
Daytime urgent threshold360Urgent outside sleep time.
Sleep warning threshold720Warning inside the sleep schedule.
Sleep urgent threshold840Urgent inside the sleep schedule.
Device offline threshold30Offline when the device has not contacted the server at all for this long. Checked before every other rule, including presence modes.

5.5 Alerts

The server creates an alert when a device enters Warning, Urgent or Offline, and will not create a duplicate while one of the same type is still pending. Open the alert list from the bell icon and tap Acknowledge once you have checked on the person. Acknowledged alerts stay in the history with their status changed.

Alerts are visible in the app and the web portal only. This version does not send SMS, email or push notifications.

6Raspberry Pi device

The device program is a single Python loop. Every second it polls the sensors; it sends a heartbeat on a timer, sends a motion or sound event when a detector fires (rate-limited by a minimum interval), and stores anything it could not deliver in a local SQLite queue that is flushed when the server is reachable again.

6.1 Hardware

Reference build: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 WH, HLK-LD2410C 24 GHz radar presence sensor on UART, and a USB microphone.

LD2410C pinRaspberry Pi pin
VCC5 V
GNDGND
TXGPIO 15 (RXD)
RXGPIO 14 (TXD)

Enable the hardware UART and disable the serial console:

sudo raspi-config
# Interface Options → Serial Port
#   Login shell over serial: No
#   Serial hardware enabled: Yes

Check the microphone is visible and records:

arecord -l
arecord -f S16_LE -c 1 -r 16000 -d 2 -t raw > /tmp/test.raw

6.2 Install and configure

cd ~/ruok_device_python           # the contents of the device/ folder
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt   # requests, pyserial
cp config/config.example.json config/config.json
nano config/config.json

Fill in the three values from the app's Add device screen and the server address:

{
  "server_url": "http://192.168.1.25:8787",
  "device_uid": "RUOK-9AC9F6",
  "device_token": "dev_...",
  "heartbeat_seconds": 60,
  "offline_flush_seconds": 20,
  "motion": { "enabled": true, "mode": "mock", "serial_port": "/dev/ttyS0",
              "baudrate": 256000, "min_interval_seconds": 30, "mock_probability": 0.25 },
  "voice":  { "enabled": true, "use_arecord": true, "threshold_rms": 500,
              "sample_seconds": 2, "interval_seconds": 30, "min_interval_seconds": 60 }
}
KeyMeaning
heartbeat_secondsHow often to tell the server the device is alive. Keep it well below the offline threshold (default 30 min).
motion.modemock generates random detections for testing without hardware; ld2410 reads the radar over UART.
motion.min_interval_secondsMinimum gap between two motion events sent to the server.
voice.threshold_rmsLoudness (RMS of 16-bit samples) above which a 2-second sample counts as sound. Raise it in a noisy room.
battery_level, wifi_strengthOptional numbers sent with each heartbeat and shown in the app.

Run it in the foreground first and watch the log:

python main.py
# R U OK? device started. server=http://192.168.1.25:8787 uid=RUOK-9AC9F6
# Sent event: heartbeat
# Sent event: motion_detected

6.3 Run on boot

sudo bash system/install_service.sh
sudo systemctl enable ruok-device
sudo systemctl start ruok-device
sudo systemctl status ruok-device
journalctl -u ruok-device -f          # live log

The service restarts automatically five seconds after any crash and waits for the network to be online before starting.

7How status is decided

Every 60 seconds, and whenever a device event arrives, the server evaluates each device in this order. The first matching rule sets the status.

OrderConditionStatus
1Alert rules switched off for this deviceAlerts off
2The device has never contacted the serverWaiting
3No contact for ≥ offline thresholdOffline
4A presence mode is activeAway Vacation Paused Maintenance
5No motion, sound or button press ever recordedWaiting
6No reaction for ≥ urgent threshold (sleep or daytime set, depending on the schedule)Urgent
7No reaction for ≥ warning thresholdWarning
8Inside the sleep schedule and within limitsSleeping
9OtherwiseNormal

Warning, Urgent and Offline each create an alert, deduplicated against any pending alert of the same type for the same device. Because the offline check comes before presence modes, a device that stops reporting during a vacation still raises an alert. That is deliberate: the box should stay online even when the house is empty.

Worked example

Default rules, sleep schedule 22:30 to 06:30, last motion at 21:00. At 00:00 the person has been still for 180 minutes. It is sleep time, so the 720-minute sleep warning applies and the status is Sleeping. If the last motion had been at 09:00 the previous morning, 900 minutes have passed, which exceeds the 840-minute sleep urgent threshold: the status becomes Urgent and an alert is created.

8API reference

All endpoints accept and return JSON. Guardian endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> from register or login. The device endpoint authenticates with two headers: X-Device-UID and X-Device-Token. Tokens expire after 7 days.

MethodPathAuthPurpose
GET/api/healthnoneLiveness check.
POST/api/auth/registernoneCreate a guardian and their family. Body: name, email, password, phone (optional).
POST/api/auth/loginnoneReturns a session token and the user record.
GET/api/meguardianCurrent user.
GET/api/devicesguardianDevices in the guardian's family, each with a computed status block.
POST/api/devicesguardianCreate a device. Returns device_uid and the one-time device_token.
GET/api/devices/{id}/statusguardianFull evaluation for one device (see section 7).
GET/api/devices/{id}/events?limit=100guardianMost recent events, newest first, up to 500.
GET / POST/api/devices/{id}/sleep-scheduleguardianRead or replace the schedule: start_time, end_time, days_of_week (0 = Monday), enabled.
GET/api/devices/{id}/presence-modesguardianLast 50 presence-mode records.
POST/api/devices/{id}/presence-modeguardianSet a mode: mode_type (home, away, vacation, pause, maintenance), start_at, end_at, note. home disables all active modes.
GET / POST/api/devices/{id}/alert-rulesguardianRead or update the five thresholds and the enabled flag.
GET/api/alertsguardianUp to 200 alerts across the family, newest first.
POST/api/alerts/{id}/acknowledgeguardianMark an alert acknowledged.
POST/api/admin/evaluate-alertsguardianRun the evaluation loop immediately.
POST/api/device-eventsdeviceReport an event: event_type (heartbeat, motion_detected, voice_detected, button_pressed), detected, value_number, value_text, timestamp, meta.

Example: device heartbeat

POST /api/device-events
X-Device-UID: RUOK-9AC9F6
X-Device-Token: dev_...
Content-Type: application/json

{ "event_type": "heartbeat", "detected": true,
  "timestamp": "2026-09-02T22:07:14",
  "meta": { "battery_level": 87, "wifi_strength": -58 } }

9Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely cause and fix
App shows Cannot reach the serverServer bound to 127.0.0.1 only, phone on a different network, or firewall. Start with RUOK_HOST=0.0.0.0, confirm the PC IP, allow port 8787.
App shows No response from the serverThe address is reachable but nothing answers within 12 seconds. Check the server console and that the port matches.
Sign-in returns Invalid or expired token on the dashboardTokens last 7 days, and change if RUOK_SECRET_KEY changes. The app signs you out automatically; sign in again.
Device stays WaitingThe Pi has not sent anything. Check config.json values, run python main.py in the foreground and read the error.
Device log says 401 UnauthorizedWrong device_uid or device_token. Create a new device in the app and copy both values again.
Device goes Offline although it is runningHeartbeat interval longer than the offline threshold, or the Pi lost Wi-Fi. Events queue locally and are re-sent when the connection returns.
Sound is never detectedarecord not installed or wrong default capture device. Test with arecord -l; lower threshold_rms.
Motion is never detected in ld2410 modeSerial console still enabled, TX/RX swapped, or wrong port. Verify with raspi-config and try /dev/serial0.
Times in the app look several hours offA database created by an older version stores creation times in UTC. Delete web/data/ruok_server.sqlite and run python setup_db.py (this removes all accounts and devices).

    lib/models/           Device, DeviceStatus, AlertItem, SleepSchedule, ...
    lib/services/         api_client.dart, local_store.dart

    test/core_test.dart   unit tests (flutter test)

    app/logic.py          status evaluation and alert creation
    app/database.py       SQLite schema
    app/security.py       password hashing, session and device tokens
    web/index.html        guardian web portal
    setup_server.ps1, run_server.ps1, setup_db.py

    sensors/              motion_ld2410.py (mock + UART), voice_detector.py

Developer checks for the app: flutter analyze and flutter test both pass on the current source. To change the default server address at build time use flutter run --dart-define=RUOK_BASE_URL=http://192.168.1.25:8787.

11Privacy and limitations

Privacy by design

  • No camera. The radar sensor reports presence and distance only.
  • No audio is stored or transmitted. The microphone sample is reduced to a single loudness number on the device and discarded.
  • The server records only event types and timestamps. All data stays on the guardian's own PC.

Known limitations of this version

  • Alerts appear in the app and portal only; there is no SMS, email or push delivery.
  • The LD2410C driver in ld2410 mode detects serial activity rather than decoding the full radar protocol. Mock mode is the fully verified path.
  • Family membership is stored but every member currently has full access to every device in the family.
  • The server speaks plain HTTP and is meant for a home network. Do not expose port 8787 to the internet without adding HTTPS and a strong RUOK_SECRET_KEY.
  • A device token cannot be re-issued; create a new device if it is lost.
